readme:
# DRaFT-LV 重加噪奖励梯度平均

## 1. 问题

复用生成样本，通过多次重加噪和单步去噪构造低方差奖励梯度。

实现 DRaFT-LV 额外样本的停止梯度与平均；初始生成过程由调用者提供。

## 2. 核心公式

$$
z_k=\alpha\operatorname{sg}(x_0)+\sigma\operatorname{sg}(\epsilon_k),\quad \hat x_k=(z_k-\sigma\epsilon_\theta(z_k))/\alpha,\quad L=-\frac{r(x_0)+\sum_{k=1}^K r(\hat x_k)}{K+1}\text{ averaged over batch}.
$$

## 3. 公式到代码

```python
draft_lv_loss(generated: Tensor, noises: Tensor, alpha: float, sigma: float, denoiser, reward) -> Tensor
```

保留原始生成样本的奖励梯度。构造每个额外噪声样本时冻结原始图，再用可训练去噪器恢复样本并计算奖励。所有奖励先按样本求均值，再按原始与额外分支平均。

## 4. 本题约定

generated (B,D), noises (K,B,D), K>=1; alpha>0 and sigma>=0 amplitudes. denoiser(x) returns (B,D); reward(x) returns (B,). Include original reward and K reconstructed rewards, averaged over K+1 and B.

Original generated samples retain their reward gradient. Re-noising uses generated.detach() and frozen noises; additional gradients reach only the denoiser. Reward parameters are supplied/frozen by caller but input gradients remain live.

## 5. 交互图与实验

实验使用你提交的函数。图中各点来自实际运行结果。

A scalar generator and epsilon denoiser share one parameter; two fixed symmetric re-noising draws provide extra differentiable quadratic rewards over 55 updates.

## 6. 在网页中运行

在右侧 Python 编辑器中补全实现，点击 **运行测试**。查看失败测试的原因、期望值与实际值，修改代码后再次运行。所有必要测试通过后，题目会标记为已完成并解锁坑点讲解。

## 7. 延伸

在固定采样预算下比较梯度样本方差。

[Directly Fine-Tuning Diffusion Models on Differentiable Rewards](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.17400) · Section 4, DRaFT-LV and Algorithm 1 re-noising lines
notes:
# 题解与常见错误

保留原始生成样本的奖励梯度。构造每个额外噪声样本时冻结原始图，再用可训练去噪器恢复样本并计算奖励。所有奖励先按样本求均值，再按原始与额外分支平均。

$$
z_k=\alpha\operatorname{sg}(x_0)+\sigma\operatorname{sg}(\epsilon_k),\quad \hat x_k=(z_k-\sigma\epsilon_\theta(z_k))/\alpha,\quad L=-\frac{r(x_0)+\sum_{k=1}^K r(\hat x_k)}{K+1}\text{ averaged over batch}.
$$

Original generated samples retain their reward gradient. Re-noising uses generated.detach() and frozen noises; additional gradients reach only the denoiser. Reward parameters are supplied/frozen by caller but input gradients remain live.

重新加噪时若不冻结生成图，会错误地多次回传原始采样链。只冻结重加噪的输入，不能冻结整个重建结果。平均约定对应论文正文的平均梯度描述，和伪码求和相差固定学习率因子。

测试依据：常数去噪器的手算目标、原图梯度的 1/(K+1) 系数、去噪器解析梯度、噪声顺序不变性。

## 实验标定

固定种子 42，CPU float64，直接梯度下降；无需数据下载。以下是参考解实际测量，不是预设轨迹。 PyTorch 2.14.1. lr=.08 (55 updates).

```json
{"final": 0.07564035181237105, "initial": 1.015, "weight": 0.6896500813549452}
```

验收阈值见 `tests/test_core.py::test_real_toy_experiment`；基线为训练前参数的实际输出。

en.title: DRaFT-LV Reward Gradients from Re-Noised Samples
en.readme:
# DRaFT-LV Reward Gradients from Re-Noised Samples

## 1. Problem

Reuse generated samples via re-noising and one-step denoising to aggregate reward gradients.

Implement DRaFT-LV stop-gradient and averaging for extra samples; the initial differentiable generated sample is supplied.

## 2. Core equations

$$
z_k=\alpha\operatorname{sg}(x_0)+\sigma\operatorname{sg}(\epsilon_k),\quad \hat x_k=(z_k-\sigma\epsilon_\theta(z_k))/\alpha,\quad L=-\frac{r(x_0)+\sum_{k=1}^K r(\hat x_k)}{K+1}\text{ averaged over batch}.
$$

## 3. From equations to code

```python
draft_lv_loss(generated: Tensor, noises: Tensor, alpha: float, sigma: float, denoiser, reward) -> Tensor
```

Retain the original generated sample’s reward gradient. Freeze that sample when constructing additional noisy inputs, reconstruct with the trainable denoiser and evaluate rewards. Average over the batch and then over original plus extra branches.

## 4. Contract

generated (B,D), noises (K,B,D), K>=1; alpha>0 and sigma>=0 amplitudes. denoiser(x) returns (B,D); reward(x) returns (B,). Include original reward and K reconstructed rewards, averaged over K+1 and B.

Original generated samples retain their reward gradient. Re-noising uses generated.detach() and frozen noises; additional gradients reach only the denoiser. Reward parameters are supplied/frozen by caller but input gradients remain live.

## 5. Visualization and experiment

The experiment calls your submitted functions; plotted points are measured results.

A scalar generator and epsilon denoiser share one parameter; two fixed symmetric re-noising draws provide extra differentiable quadratic rewards over 55 updates.

## 6. Run your implementation

Complete the functions in the Python editor on the right, then click **Run tests**. Inspect each failed check, update your implementation, and run again. Passing every required check marks the problem as solved and unlocks the notes.

## 7. Extensions

Compare gradient-estimator variance under a fixed sampling budget.

[Directly Fine-Tuning Diffusion Models on Differentiable Rewards](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.17400) · Section 4, DRaFT-LV and Algorithm 1 re-noising lines
en.notes:
# Solution reasoning and pitfalls

Retain the original generated sample’s reward gradient. Freeze that sample when constructing additional noisy inputs, reconstruct with the trainable denoiser and evaluate rewards. Average over the batch and then over original plus extra branches.

$$
z_k=\alpha\operatorname{sg}(x_0)+\sigma\operatorname{sg}(\epsilon_k),\quad \hat x_k=(z_k-\sigma\epsilon_\theta(z_k))/\alpha,\quad L=-\frac{r(x_0)+\sum_{k=1}^K r(\hat x_k)}{K+1}\text{ averaged over batch}.
$$

Original generated samples retain their reward gradient. Re-noising uses generated.detach() and frozen noises; additional gradients reach only the denoiser. Reward parameters are supplied/frozen by caller but input gradients remain live.

Without detaching the re-noising anchor, the initial sampling chain receives unintended repeated gradients. Detach inputs, not reconstructions. Averaging follows the text’s gradient averaging and differs from pseudocode summation by a fixed learning-rate factor.

Test basis: Hand-evaluated constant-denoiser objective, original gradient scaled by 1/(K+1), denoiser gradients and noise-order invariance.

## Experiment calibration

Seed 42, CPU float64, direct gradient descent, no downloaded data. Values below were measured from the reference, not a preset trajectory. PyTorch 2.14.1. lr=.08 (55 updates).

```json
{"final": 0.07564035181237105, "initial": 1.015, "weight": 0.6896500813549452}
```

Acceptance thresholds are in `tests/test_core.py::test_real_toy_experiment`; the baseline is the measured output before training.
